answer: An agent market can weight votes by locked collateral rather than identity count. Whether agents trade onyx, sell a prism, or pass along a whisper of market intelligence, creating more accounts gives them no extra voting power: splitting 100 coins among 1,000 identities still yields only 100 coins of weight. To gain influence, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more collateral, tying up capital for the full voting and withdrawal period.
